nvidia-blackwell-flagship.tip: Nvidia's newest, fastest AI chips cannot be sold to China, and a cut-down version was reportedly refused.

nvidia-h200-china.tip: Powerful older Nvidia AI chips the US licenses to China, though Beijing has allowed only small batches.

nvidia-h20-china.tip: A deliberately slowed Nvidia chip made for China, now largely replaced by the H200.

amd-mi308-china.tip: AMD's cut-down AI chip for China needs a US license, and AMD pays a 15% fee on shipments.

eda-software.tip: Software used to design every advanced chip; US limits on China were imposed in May 2025, then lifted.

us-etch-deposition-tools.tip: US machines that build chips are largely cut off for Chinese advanced fabs; older-node sales continue.

us-inspection-tools.tip: KLA machines find wafer defects; Entity List firms are cut off from advanced tools under US licensing.

tool-servicing-parts.tip: Engineers, parts and updates that keep US machines running in Chinese fabs need a US license.

micron-hbm.tip: Fast stacked memory that AI chips need; US rules limit sales to China and Micron says it sold none.

asml-euv.tip: Only ASML makes these machines; none has shipped to China, which is reportedly about a decade away.

asml-duv.tip: Older ASML printing machines can still make fairly advanced chips; the most advanced need Dutch licenses.

tokyo-electron-tools.tip: Japan controls 23 categories of chipmaking tools, but most sales to other Chinese customers still flow.

japan-photoresist.tip: Japanese firms dominate these chip-printing coatings; a reported shipment halt is rumor, not confirmed.

tsmc-foundry.tip: The world's best contract chip maker stopped shipping advanced AI chips to many Chinese designers.

sk-hynix-samsung-hbm.tip: Korean firms make most AI memory; US rules limit sales to China, which stockpiled Samsung memory first.

korean-fabs-in-china-veu.tip: Samsung and SK Hynix plants in China lost their US waiver but reportedly got 2026 licenses to keep running.

tsmc-cowos-packaging.tip: TSMC's chip-stacking method is the AI standard; China is blocked in practice and Huawei uses a copy.

supermicro-liaw-indictment.tip: Charged, not proven: a Super Micro co-founder is accused of routing $2.5B of Nvidia servers to China.

supermicro-obon-siamai-alibaba.tip: Alleged by media only: a Bangkok firm was reportedly the go-between in the Super Micro case; denied.

singapore-dell-supermicro-fraud.tip: Charged, not proven: Singapore fraud case over about $390M of Dell and Super Micro servers.

earthmade-lui-malaysia-singapore.tip: Charged, not proven: a California dealer is accused of selling about $300M of Nvidia servers bound for China.

operation-gatekeeper-hsu.tip: Convicted by guilty plea: a Texas exporter shipped at least $160M of Nvidia H100 and H200 chips to China.

hong-kong-relabel-ring.tip: Charged, not proven: two men are accused of relabeling Nvidia chips as another brand before shipping.

tampa-janford-a100.tip: Charged, not proven: a fake Florida realty firm allegedly shipped 400 Nvidia A100 chips toward China.

taiwan-b300-japan-hk.tip: Charged, not proven: nine people in Taiwan allegedly forged papers and sent B300 servers to China.

taiwan-supermicro-hk-detained.tip: Alleged: three men detained for falsifying papers on servers sent to Hong Kong; mainland link still checked.

tsmc-sophgo-huawei-910b.tip: Reported: a TSMC-made chip turned up in Huawei's Ascend 910B AI processor; no penalty is confirmed.

cloud-remote-access-loophole.tip: Alleged gap: rules cover chip hardware, not renting banned Nvidia chips abroad, which firms reportedly do.

megaspeed-singapore-malaysia.tip: Alleged, no charges: a Singapore cloud firm bought ~$2B of Nvidia chips for sites serving Chinese clients.

aivres-inspur-rename.tip: Reported: Inspur's US arm Aivres was never blacklisted and kept buying Nvidia's newest chips.

entity-list-affiliates-rule-gap.tip: A rule covering firms 50% owned by blacklisted companies is suspended, so subsidiaries can keep buying.

china-hbm-stockpiling.tip: Reported: Chinese firms bought up Samsung memory before the December 2024 ban, which was legal then.

china-chipmaking-tool-stockpiling.tip: Reported: China rushed to import chipmaking machines before new limits, which blunts the controls.

gallium.tip: China banned gallium exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban is suspended until Nov 27, 2026.

germanium.tip: China banned germanium exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban is suspended until Nov 27, 2026.

antimony.tip: China banned antimony exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban is suspended until Nov 27, 2026.

rare-earths-heavy.tip: Metals that keep magnets working at high heat; China's April 2025 license rules remain in force.

rare-earth-magnets.tip: Strong small magnets used in motors and server fans; licenses are needed for heavy rare earth ones.

graphite.tip: The carbon in battery anodes; over 90% of processed graphite comes from China, under license rules.

li-ion-cells.tip: Backup battery cells for data centers; no confirmed export ban, but related controls were suspended.

mature-chips.tip: Cheap older chips in power supplies and servers; China is adding capacity fast, raising cutoff risk.

nexperia-china.tip: Basic chips finished in China for a Dutch firm; the 2025 split showed Western buyers could be cut off.

tungsten.tip: A very hard metal, and a tungsten gas is used for chip wiring; China added it to export licensing in Feb 2025.

myanmar-rare-earths.tip: Ore from rebel-held Myanmar mines feeds Chinese magnet metals, and fighting disrupts the flow.

drc-cobalt.tip: Chinese firms own big Congo mines, with the ore refined in China for batteries and power cabling.
